disclaimer: Neufert-grade dimensional standards (C8). This is design data, not a building code. No legal code-compliance claim is made or implied by any value in this file. Values are cited to their source so that a Practitioner can check them; they are not a substitute for checking them.

units.note: All lengths are integer millimetres. All areas are square metres to one decimal. No imperial units appear in this file; imperial-native sources are converted once, at ingest, and the original value is recorded in the source note.

value_format.description: Every constrained value is an object, never a bare number, so that provenance survives.

keys.v: the value, in the unit declared for its field
keys.ref: clause / table / paragraph within that source
keys.note: optional; required when conf is derived or engine_choice

conf_meanings.verified: read directly from the primary document named in `src`
conf_meanings.reported: a credible third party attributes this value to `src`; not read first-hand
conf_meanings.derived: computed from a verified value by a stated rule (e.g. area / width)
conf_meanings.engine_choice: no source dictates this; the engine picks it, and `note` says why

flag_semantics.comment: These four booleans are consumed by the acceptance validator (ticket 07) and the brief defaulting rules (ticket 10). They are DEFINITIONS, not measurements — no reference work supplies them as such. Getting them wrong silently breaks predicates, so each is defined operationally here.
flag_semantics.is_habitable: A room intended for sustained occupation: sleeping, living, dining, working. Drives the window requirement and the exterior-wall requirement (C6 item 4). NOT the same as any national legal definition of 'habitable room' — see the findings doc, section on the kitchen disagreement.
flag_semantics.is_wet: A room containing a plumbed fixture (WC, basin, bath, shower, sink, washing machine). Drives wet-room clustering (C6 item 5).
flag_semantics.is_private: A room that must not lie on the circulation path to any other room. Drives the reachability predicate (C6 item 1): the entry-to-room graph may not route through a room where is_private is true.
flag_semantics.needs_window: The room must have at least one window on an exterior wall. Set true wherever is_habitable is true. This is an ENGINE DECISION, not a universal rule — England's Building Regulations impose no daylight requirement at all (see findings). We impose one because a Homeowner judges by 'would I live here'.

region_model.comment: See the findings doc for the argument. Short version: the corpus splits into a body-derived layer that does not vary by region, and a convention-derived layer that varies so much that blending it produces buildings belonging to no tradition. `region` selects the second layer only.
region_model.default_region_rationale: C8 names Neufert as the posture and the primary geometry corpus (Swiss Dwellings) is DE/CH. The model proposes in a European convention (C10); the constraints it is projected onto must be in the same convention or the projection fights the proposal.
region_model.verification_region_rationale: Every UK number here was read first-hand from a Crown-copyright document published under the Open Government Licence v3.0. It is the only profile that is free, complete, and independently checkable end-to-end, so it is the profile the test suite asserts against.
region_model.must_match: The region enum here MUST be the same enum as the training-data conditioning variable in ticket 06. If the model is conditioned on region and the constraints are not, the solver projects a region-A proposal onto region-B constraints, which is strictly worse than either alone.

tier_model.comment: A single number per cell is not recoverable from the sources; England alone yields five different 'minimum bedroom areas' depending on which instrument you invoke. Tier disambiguates.

tiers.statutory_floor: The hardest number any instrument in that region imposes. Below this a plan is rejected. Deliberately permissive — it is a floor, not a goal.
tiers.market_default: What is actually built and what a Homeowner expects. This is what unstated brief fields default to (ticket 10) and what the solver targets.
tiers.accessible: The region's wheelchair-user tier. Not a v1 default; carried so that adopting it later is a parameter change, not a rewrite.

tier_model.default_tier_rationale: C2 says the Homeowner judges by 'would I live here'. A plan built to the statutory floor is legal and unliveable. Defaulting to the floor would make the engine reliably produce plans nobody wants.

validator_binding.comment: This is the C10 split expressed in data: statutory_floor is a hard constraint, market_default is a soft objective. Ticket 07's 'hard or soft' question is answered per-value by which tier the number came from, not by a separate flag.
